say: Emergency scams say a loved one is arrested or injured. Voices can even be imitated with software today. So agree a simple family code word.

panel.heading: Mama Tolu and the family code word
items: Agree a secret family word, not on social media
Emergency caller? Ask: what is our word?
No word? Say you will call back, and hang up
Call your relative's normal number

say: A phone with no lock is an open purse. Use a PIN of at least six digits, or your fingerprint.

panel.heading: Layers that protect your money
items: Screen lock: a PIN of at least six digits
Different PINs for card and app, not 1234
A lower daily transfer limit
Debit alerts on, and know the card freeze
Most savings in a separate account

say: Use different PINs for your card and your app. Not your birthday, phone number or 1234. And never save PINs in your phone notes.

say: Set a lower daily transfer limit. If a criminal gets in, he can take less. Raise it only when you need to.

say: Your email can reset your other accounts. Your WhatsApp can be used to ask all your contacts for money.
A friend's hacked account says, I sent you a code by mistake, please send it. That is your own WhatsApp code. Sharing it hands over your account.

panel.heading: Weak setup or strong setup?
left: Sharing a code a friend asks for

say: Use three or four unrelated words with a number. Turn on two-step verification. Ifeoma lost her WhatsApp after sharing a code. She registered her number again, warned her contacts, and set her own PIN. Nobody sent money.

panel.heading: Weak setup or strong setup?
left: Sharing a code a friend asks for

say: Older relatives need three rules they can remember under pressure. First, no codes and no PINs, to anyone.

cards.d: To anyone. If someone asks, hang up.
No money for emergencies until you call the person directly, or the code word is given.
One trusted number to call before any payment.

say: Second, no money for an emergency until you call the person directly.

cards.d: To anyone. If someone asks, hang up.

say: Third, when in doubt, call me. Write the rules on a card and stick it near their phone.

say: Tell customers which account you use, and that you will never change it by message.
A cooperative of 60 women in Owerri shares checked warnings in three lines: what happened, the red flag, what to do. Within three months, two members stopped a fake bank call.

panel.heading: Protect customers and community
items: Tell customers your one official account
Say you will never ask for PIN or OTP
Search monthly for copycat pages
Warn in three lines: what, red flag, action
Support victims; never shame them

say: To remember. Find contacts yourself. Agree a family code word. Lower your limits and turn on alerts.
Turn on two-step verification. And spread protection, not panic.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Find contacts yourself, never from the message
A family code word stops emergency scams
Lower limits, debit alerts, a card freeze
Two-step verification on WhatsApp and email
Teach three rules; warn without panic

say: Now practise. Save your official numbers and agree a code word, check your limits and alerts, turn on two-step verification, and teach one relative the three rules.
